title: At least 139 migrants dead, including some children, after boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes, UN agency says
gist: Reuters via Al-Monitor: at least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, died and about 84 are missing after a boat carrying 305 people capsized off Obock, Djibouti, on its way to Yemen. The IOM says traffic on the Eastern Route toward the Gulf continues despite Yemen's worst fighting since 2022 and renewed conflict in Ethiopia's Tigray.

insights.claim: At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, died and around 84 went missing when a boat carrying 305 people capsized near Guhere, north of Obock in Djibouti, on the night of October 8-9, 2026, while heading to Yemen.
insights.so_what: One of the deadliest incidents on the Red Sea migration corridor, adding to humanitarian pressure in a conflict zone.
insights.quote: At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Around 82 people survived the Djibouti-Yemen shipwreck, and Djiboutian authorities continued search and rescue while providing medical care and arranging burials.
insights.so_what: Gives the scale of the incident and the local response capacity.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: Migrants keep crossing to Yemen hoping to reach wealthier Gulf countries even though Yemen is seeing its most serious fighting between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis since the UN-brokered 2022 truce.
insights.so_what: Economic pull from Gulf labour markets outweighs war risk, so flows and humanitarian costs persist.

insights.claim: In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the Eastern Route while the number of people making the journey rose by 18%, according to IOM's Missing Migrants Project.
insights.so_what: Rising volume on a deadly route points to deepening economic and security stress in the Horn of Africa.
insights.quote: In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the route, according to IOM’s Missing Migrants Project, as the number of people undertaking the journey increased by 18%.

insights.claim: An IOM official said migrants keep using the Eastern Route as conditions in Ethiopia and Yemen change, though the volume and direction of movement can shift over time.
insights.so_what: Migration flows respond to conflict and economic conditions at both ends of the corridor.
